disable_condition: Disable ONLY if you do not rely on instant file-content search in Start Menu or File Explorer
purpose: Windows Search Indexer (SearchIndexer.exe) — continuously crawls drives to index filenames and file contents.
rationale: Frequent top Disk I/O and CPU consumer that also amplifies antivirus real-time scans; alternatively exclude developer/VM folders in Indexing Options.

disable_condition: Disable if you have an NVMe/SSD and ample RAM and want lower background disk churn
purpose: SysMain (formerly Superfetch) — analyzes launch patterns and preloads application files into RAM.
rationale: Provides minimal launch speedup on modern NVMe SSD + high-RAM PCs while generating continuous background read/write I/O.

disable_condition: Disable if you do not use local Windows 11 AI / Copilot+ background features
purpose: Windows AI Components Host — background runtime hosting local Windows 11 AI fabric services.
rationale: Runs automatically at boot on newer Windows 11 builds even when local AI features are unused.

disable_condition: Disable ONLY if you never print to physical printers and do not use 'Microsoft Print to PDF'
purpose: Print Spooler — queues print jobs to physical printers and virtual print drivers.
rationale: Frees permanent boot RAM and eliminates historic Print Spooler privilege-escalation/RCE surface when printing is unused.

disable_condition: Disable ONLY if you never print to physical printers
purpose: Printer Extensions and Notifications — displays custom OEM printer status dialogs.
rationale: Unneeded when physical printers are not used.

disable_condition: Disable if you do not connect a USB flatbed document scanner or WIA camera
purpose: Windows Image Acquisition (WIA) — interfaces with legacy WIA flatbed scanners and USB cameras.
rationale: Often configured as Automatic at boot even when no scanner hardware is attached.

disable_condition: Disable if you do not use a WIA document scanner
purpose: Still Image Acquisition Events — dispatches hardware button presses from connected WIA scanners.
rationale: Unneeded without a dedicated USB scanner.

disable_condition: Disable if you do not plug in a physical corporate/government Smart Card (PIV/CAC) reader
purpose: Smart Card — manages access to physical Smart Card hardware readers.
rationale: Frequently runs in the background polling for physical Smart Card readers on personal PCs.

disable_condition: Disable if you do not use a physical Smart Card reader
purpose: Smart Card Device Enumeration — creates virtual Plug-and-Play nodes for Smart Card readers.
rationale: Unneeded unless a physical Smart Card reader is attached.

disable_condition: Disable if you do not use a physical Smart Card reader
purpose: Smart Card Removal Policy — locks the desktop when a corporate Smart Card is removed.
rationale: Unneeded without physical Smart Card authentication.

disable_condition: Disable if you do not use a physical Smart Card reader
purpose: Certificate Propagation — copies X.509 certificates from inserted physical Smart Cards into the user store.
rationale: Often wakes and stays resident in RAM even when no Smart Card reader exists.

disable_condition: Disable ONLY if you do not use Xbox controllers/accessories or Xbox PC apps
purpose: Xbox Service — background companion daemon supporting Xbox accessories and integration.
rationale: Runs automatically at boot on systems with Xbox redistributables installed.

disable_condition: Disable ONLY if you do not play Xbox App, PC Game Pass, or Xbox Live sign-in games
purpose: Xbox Live Auth Manager — authenticates Microsoft accounts with Xbox Live services in games.
rationale: Unneeded if you only play non-Xbox games (e.g., standalone Steam/GOG titles without Xbox sign-in) or don't game.

disable_condition: Disable ONLY if you do not use Xbox Cloud Saves or PC Game Pass
purpose: Xbox Live Game Save — synchronizes cloud save files for Xbox Play Anywhere and Game Pass titles.
rationale: Unneeded when Xbox/Game Pass titles are not played.

disable_condition: Disable ONLY if you do not use Xbox Wireless Adapters or Xbox accessories
purpose: Xbox Accessory Management Service — manages Xbox controller accessory protocols.
rationale: Unneeded without Xbox controller accessories.

disable_condition: Disable ONLY if you do not play Xbox Live multiplayer PC games
purpose: Xbox Live Networking Service — provides peer-to-peer multiplayer networking helpers for Xbox Live.
rationale: Unneeded when Xbox Live multiplayer is unused.

disable_condition: Disable if you do not pair your smartphone with Microsoft Phone Link
purpose: Phone Service — manages telephony state and backs Microsoft Phone Link integration.
rationale: Phone Link's companion host (PhoneExperienceHost.exe) frequently consumes 300–600 MB of background RAM.

disable_condition: Disable if you do not need desktop apps (Weather/Maps) tracking physical Wi-Fi/GPS location
purpose: Geolocation Service — estimates physical device coordinates via Wi-Fi/GPS triangulation.
rationale: Eliminates background location polling when desktop geolocation apps are unused.

disable_condition: Disable if you are not actively managing Windows Insider preview flight builds
purpose: Windows Insider Service — manages enrollment and flighting for the Windows Insider Program.
rationale: Unneeded on stable builds or when you are not actively pulling Insider preview updates.

disable_condition: Disable if you do not want Windows automatically configuring newly discovered smart devices on Wi-Fi
purpose: Network Connected Devices Auto-Setup — watches private networks to auto-install UPnP/WSD smart devices.
rationale: Prevents unsolicited smart-device driver installations and trims background LAN listener overhead.

disable_condition: Disable if you never turn your PC into a Wi-Fi Mobile Hotspot for other devices
purpose: Windows Mobile Hotspot Service — shares your PC's internet connection over a virtual Wi-Fi AP.
rationale: Unneeded if you never broadcast a Mobile Hotspot from your PC.

disable_condition: Disable ONLY if you do not use Windows Hello Fingerprint or Facial Recognition sign-in
purpose: Windows Biometric Service — captures and matches fingerprint and IR facial biometric data.
rationale: Safe to disable on desktops or laptops without fingerprint/IR-face sensors (PIN login still works).

disable_condition: Disable ONLY if you never connect INTO this PC via Windows Remote Desktop (RDP)
purpose: Remote Desktop Services — hosts incoming RDP remote desktop sessions.
rationale: Improves security posture and saves resources when incoming RDP hosting is unused.

disable_condition: Disable ONLY if you never host incoming Windows Remote Desktop (RDP) sessions
purpose: Remote Desktop Configuration — manages session configuration for incoming RDP connections.
rationale: Companion service to Remote Desktop hosting.

disable_condition: Disable ONLY if you never host incoming Windows Remote Desktop (RDP) sessions
purpose: Remote Desktop Services UserMode Port Redirector — redirects printers/drives over RDP.
rationale: Companion service to Remote Desktop hosting.

disable_condition: Disable if you do not use legacy Windows Wallet or NFC tap-to-pay
purpose: WalletService — legacy payment/wallet card storage broker.
rationale: Obsolete on virtually all desktop and laptop PCs.

disable_condition: Disable if your PC does not use NFC tap-to-pay secure elements
purpose: Payments and NFC/SE Manager — manages Near Field Communication (NFC) secure payment elements.
rationale: Unneeded on laptops and desktops without NFC payment hardware.

disable_condition: Disable if Windows is running on physical bare-metal hardware (NOT inside a Hyper-V VM)
purpose: Hyper-V Guest Service Interface — used only when this Windows OS is a guest VM inside Hyper-V.
rationale: Does nothing on bare-metal physical PCs (note: WSL2 on the host uses vmcompute/HvHost, not vmic*).

disable_condition: Disable if Windows is running on physical bare-metal hardware (NOT inside a Hyper-V VM)
purpose: Hyper-V Heartbeat Service — reports guest VM liveness to a parent Hyper-V host.
rationale: Unneeded on bare-metal physical PCs.

disable_condition: Disable if Windows is running on physical bare-metal hardware (NOT inside a Hyper-V VM)
purpose: Hyper-V Data Exchange Service — exchanges key-value metadata with a parent Hyper-V host.
rationale: Unneeded on bare-metal physical PCs.

disable_condition: Disable if Windows is running on physical bare-metal hardware (NOT inside a Hyper-V VM)
purpose: Hyper-V Remote Desktop Virtualization — supports Enhanced Session Mode inside a Hyper-V guest.
rationale: Unneeded on bare-metal physical PCs.

disable_condition: Disable if Windows is running on physical bare-metal hardware (NOT inside a Hyper-V VM)
purpose: Hyper-V Guest Shutdown Service — allows a parent Hyper-V host to shut down a guest VM.
rationale: Unneeded on bare-metal physical PCs.

disable_condition: Disable if Windows is running on physical bare-metal hardware (NOT inside a Hyper-V VM)
purpose: Hyper-V Time Synchronization — syncs guest VM clock with a parent Hyper-V host.
rationale: Unneeded on bare-metal physical PCs.

disable_condition: Disable if Windows is running on physical bare-metal hardware (NOT inside a Hyper-V VM)
purpose: Hyper-V PowerShell Direct Service — enables PowerShell Direct into a Hyper-V guest VM.
rationale: Unneeded on bare-metal physical PCs.

disable_condition: Disable if Windows is running on physical bare-metal hardware (NOT inside a Hyper-V VM)
purpose: Hyper-V Volume Shadow Copy Requestor — coordinates host-initiated backups inside a Hyper-V guest.
rationale: Unneeded on bare-metal physical PCs.

disable_condition: Disable if you do not use Western Digital Drive Utilities (LED control, RAID, or password unlock)
purpose: WD Drive Manager — polls attached WD/SanDisk external drives for temperature, RAID, and LED status.
rationale: Standard USB/NVMe external drives read and write natively via Windows storage drivers without constant background polling.

disable_condition: Disable if your ASUS laptop does not have (or you never use) the virtual LED numpad on the touchpad
purpose: ASUS NumberPad Driver Service — powers the touch-illuminated numeric keypad embedded in ASUS touchpads.
rationale: Polls touchpad coordinates continuously from boot even if you never toggle the touchpad numpad.

disable_condition: Disable if you use Ethernet or prefer standard Wi-Fi card driver antenna management
purpose: ASUS MultiAntenna Service — dynamically tunes Wi-Fi antenna diversity on ASUS ROG laptops.
rationale: Optional OEM wireless heuristic daemon (~19 MB RAM).

disable_condition: Disable (or uninstall McAfee) ONLY if Microsoft Defender or another primary antivirus is actively protecting your PC
purpose: McAfee Access Protection Service — OEM trial or third-party McAfee background protection process.
rationale: Running leftover OEM McAfee services concurrently with active Microsoft Defender causes severe dual-antivirus file-hook contention.

disable_condition: Disable (or uninstall McAfee) ONLY if Microsoft Defender or another primary antivirus is actively protecting your PC
purpose: McAfee Management Service Controller — core daemon orchestrating McAfee SystemCore modules.
rationale: Eliminates dual-antivirus contention when Microsoft Defender is your active primary antivirus.

disable_condition: Disable (or uninstall McAfee) ONLY if Microsoft Defender or another primary antivirus is actively protecting your PC
purpose: McAfee Validation Trust Protection — verifies binary signatures for McAfee SystemCore modules.
rationale: Unneeded when leftover OEM McAfee is replaced by Microsoft Defender.

disable_condition: Disable (or uninstall McAfee) ONLY if Windows Defender Firewall or another primary firewall is active
purpose: McAfee Firewall Core Service — McAfee host firewall module.
rationale: Redundant when Windows Defender Firewall (mpssvc) is active.

disable_condition: Disable (or uninstall McAfee) ONLY if you do not use an active paid McAfee subscription
purpose: McAfee Activation Service — checks OEM trial and subscription activation status.
rationale: Unneeded background trial activation daemon.

disable_condition: Disable if you rely on built-in browser Safe Browsing and Windows SmartScreen
purpose: McAfee WebAdvisor — background URL reputation helper for web browsers.
rationale: Redundant with Chromium/Firefox Safe Browsing and Windows SmartScreen.
